egygoo.tip: Loud honking and hissing, usually from a pair.

blaplo1.tip: Sharp "tink-tink-tink", like a blacksmith's hammer on an anvil.

reedov1.tip: "I AM... a red-eyed dove": two notes, a pause, then four.

capwea1.tip: Harsh, wheezy swizzling chatter around the nests.

affeag1.tip: Ringing, far-carrying "weee-ah, hyo-hyo-hyo" with the head thrown back: the sound of African rivers and dams.

redbis.tip: Male's fizzing, sizzling, buzzy song from reeds.

fisfly1.tip: Soft, high, scratchy twittering; much gentler than Southern Fiscal's harsh notes.

blhher1.tip: Mostly quiet; harsh croaking "kaaark" in flight and loud clattering at nests.

capbul1.tip: Cheerful, liquid whistles "piet-piet-patata"; harsh chatter when alarmed. Shorter, quicker phrases than Olive Thrush.

helgui.tip: Harsh, rattling "kek-kek-kek-krrrrr" from the flock, and a repeated "buck-wheat".

capfra2.tip: Loud, harsh crowing "cackalac-cackalac", mostly at dawn and dusk.

categr1.tip: Mostly silent; low "rick-rack" croaks at roosts and nesting colonies.

capsug1.tip: Scratchy, grating chatter with metallic notes; wings "frrrt" in display flight.

sybhor1.tip: Hollow "tok-tok-tok" that speeds up, the bird bowing with wings half open.

fotdro5.tip: Metallic twangs and squeaks; a great mimic, often calling before dawn.

soufis1.tip: Harsh "gzzzt" scold; song mixes grating notes with sweet whistles and mimicry.

rindov.tip: "Work HAR-der, work HAR-der", over and over.

laudov1.tip: Soft, chuckling "coo-coo-COO-coo-coo" that rises and falls, like a quiet laugh.

pitwhy.tip: Male's sharp, sibilant "tseet-tseet-tseet" while bouncing in display over a female.

afrsto1.tip: Scratchy short song; call like two stones knocked together: "weet-tsak-tsak".

sghspa2.tip: Simple "cheep, chirp" chirps, like a House Sparrow but softer.

eursta.tip: Wheezes, clicks, whistles and mimicry run together; long falling "sheeeooo" whistle.

hadibi1.tip: Loud, raucous "ha-ha-ha-de-dah", often in flight at dawn and dusk.

soghor1.tip: Deep booming "oomph, oomph" at dawn, easily mistaken for a distant lion.

sdcsun3.tip: Fast, high, jumbled twittering; sharp "tchik-tchik" calls.

whtswa3.tip: Pleasant twittering song and short "vit" calls, usually near water.

spoeao2.tip: Soft hoots at night: "hoo-hoo" from the male, answered "hoo-hoo-hoo".

spemou2.tip: Twittering "tsik-tsik" chatter from the group as they fly from bush to bush.

rewsta1.tip: Loud, melodious whistled "cher-leeeoo"; flocks very vocal.

ostric2.tip: Deep booming roar at night, like a lion.

crolap1.tip: Shrill, scratchy "kreeep" calls, also at night.

grests1.tip: Soft, twittering, slightly guttural song; quieter than Lesser Striped Swallow's nasal notes.

capwhe2.tip: Thin, warbled twittering; flocks keep up soft "tseee" contact calls.

spepig1.tip: Deep, booming "hooo-hooo-hooo" rising then falling, from roofs and cliffs.

soubou1.tip: A pair duets so fast it sounds like one bird: a clear whistle answered at once by a croak or click.

carcha1.tip: Short sweet phrases "cheroo-weet-weet", often with mimicry; growling "wur-da-wur" alarm.

blcbar1.tip: A pair duets "too-puddly, too-puddly", bobbing as they call.

whnrav1.tip: Deep, harsh croaking "kraak"; also higher, falsetto notes.

afrpip1.tip: Repeated "chrip-chrip-chrip" in display flight; "chissik" flight call.

afdfly1.tip: Very thin, high, single "tseeet" notes, like a squeaky gate; not a warbled twitter like Cape White-eye.

capcan1.tip: Long, fast, rolling canary song full of trills, from tree tops.

eswdov1.tip: Slow, sad hoots that speed up and tumble down: "my mother is dead, my father is dead, all my relatives are dead, oh, oh, oh-oh-oh".

blbpuf2.tip: Sharp "chick-weeu" and loud clicks; wings make a soft "puff" in display.

amesun2.tip: Long, fast twittering song; sharp "tsip" calls.

barswa.tip: Twittering, chattering song and "vit-vit" calls. Summer visitor.

comwax.tip: Nasal, twanging "chip-chip-tcheeer" from flocks in long grass.

crebar1.tip: Long, even trill that goes on and on, like an old alarm clock.

swewax3.tip: Says its name: soft, high "swee-swee" from small flocks.

rocmar5.tip: Mostly silent; soft twittering near cliffs and buildings.

grewoo2.tip: A group cackling together, building to a frenzy, like a crowd of laughing people.

swafra2.tip: Harsh, grating "krraae-krraae-krraae" from a perch at dawn and dusk.

didcuc1.tip: Says its name: a clear, rising "dee-dee-dee-deederik".

yelbis1.tip: Male's sizzling, buzzy display song; harsh "zeet" calls.

sptkne1.tip: At night: "ti-ti-ti-TEE-TEE-TEE-ti-ti-ti", rising then falling away.

truhor1.tip: Loud wailing, like a crying baby.

pipcis2.tip: Monotonous fast "tee-tee-tee-tee" from a bush top, going on and on.

olithr2.tip: Clear, fluty phrases, each often repeated; slower and more deliberate than Cape Robin-Chat or Cape Bulbul. Thin "tseep" call.

somgre1.tip: A loud "Willie!" from deep in a bush, often followed by a bubbling phrase: "Willie, come out and fight... scaaared".

capbat10.tip: Clear, slow whistles on one pitch plus frog-like rattling "chrrr" calls.

batapa2.tip: Loud, fast "tlip-tlip-tlip"; pairs duet, one answering the other at a different pitch.

gdcsun2.tip: Fast, jumbled, scratchy song; harsh "tchik" calls. A little slower and lower than Southern Double-collared.

armbab1.tip: A group's raucous, cackling chatter, all calling at once.

rampig1.tip: Deep, gruff cooing from the forest canopy; loud wing clatter when it flies off.

runlar1.tip: Plaintive whistled "tsee-tseeoo" from the top of a bush.

chibat1.tip: Three falling notes, like "three blind mice".

sthsee2.tip: Slow, sweet, rambling song of clear whistles and twitters.

capgra1.tip: A few slow notes, then a fast jumble of tinkling notes from a grass or bush top.

grbcam1.tip: Goat-like bleat "neeehh" and a loud snapping "tic-tic-tic".

wookin1.tip: "Tri-trrrrrrrr": one sharp note then a long falling trill.

whbcou3.tip: Bubbling "doo-doo-doo..." that falls then rises, like water poured from a bottle. Often calls before rain.

pesowl1.tip: A run of whistles rising in pitch, then loud falling "tseeu, tseeu" notes, often by day.

klacuc1.tip: Plaintive "may-tee, may-tee", repeated over and over.

brican1.tip: Rich, slow, deep canary song; heavier than Cape Canary's.

whrswi1.tip: Mostly quiet; soft twittering at nests under bridges and eaves.

wbrcha2.tip: Rising crescendo, louder each time: "it's-up-to-YOU, it's-up-to-YOU".

forcan1.tip: Soft, rambling canary twitter; quieter and thinner than Cape Canary.

reccuc1.tip: Three loud falling notes, "it-will-rain", repeated all day (and night) in summer.

bbgsta1.tip: Noisy, harsh, squeaky chattering with whistles, from flocks high in the forest.

finnig1.tip: Tremulous whistle at night: "Good Lord, deliver us".

moubuz3.tip: Thin, high, mewing "peee-oo" over the forest.

afpswi1.tip: Thin, high, twittering screams around palm trees.

zitcis1.tip: "Zit... zit... zit" with each dip of its bouncing display flight.

oliwoo2.tip: Sharp "wir-rit" double note and squeaky calls; seldom drums.

blkcus1.tip: Long, insect-like trill "trrrrrrr" lasting several seconds.

bkbbus1.tip: A short "kwick", a pause, then a "pop" like a cork from a bottle.

terbro1.tip: Chattering, grumbling "chuck-chuck-chirrr" from parties in the undergrowth.

plbpip1.tip: Repeated two-note song from a perch; hard to tell from African Pipit.

renfra1.tip: Loud, harsh crowing "kraaa-kraaa-kraaa", fading away, at dawn and dusk.

afsowl1.tip: Frog-like "prrrp" every few seconds, all night.

tamdov1.tip: Long run of soft "du-du-du" coos, slow then faster and fading, staying on one pitch (Emerald-spotted Wood Dove's falls away at the end).

gyhbus1.tip: Long, mournful "hooooo", hence its nickname "ghost bird".

alpswi1.tip: Loud, shrill trilling screams from flocks, falling in pitch.

brubru1.tip: Trilled "prrrrrrt", like an old telephone ringing.

knytur1.tip: Hoarse, croaking "kow-kow-kow-kow" from the forest canopy.

trobou1.tip: A pair duets so fast it sounds like one bird: bell-like whistles answered at once by a croak.

afbwar1.tip: Dry "trrp-trrp-trrp" notes speeding up into a rattle, like a bouncing ball, often with wing-snaps, from reedbeds.

blksaw1.tip: Mostly quiet; soft "chrrp" calls while hawking along forest edges.

nartro1.tip: Deep, hoarse "hoo-hoo" repeated, the throat puffing out.

chrcha1.tip: Rich song full of mimicry, the forest's best mimic; plaintive "toy-toy-toy" call.

afffin.tip: Fast, rolling "trrrrt" trill and a clear "vee-vee" call.

olibus1.tip: Ringing, fluty "tew-tew-tew-tew" whistles and a harsh churr.

blacuc1.tip: Mournful "I'm so sick", repeated, the last note slurred upward.

afwowl1.tip: "Who-are-YOU... who-who", in the forest at night.

viswar1.tip: Loud, sweet, accelerating song from dense fynbos; very hard to see.

afcfly1.tip: Rasping, buzzy scolds and a fast, sweet twittering song.

yeftin1.tip: Endless "tink-tink-tink", like a tiny hammer on metal.

afrswi1.tip: Shrill screams around cliffs, flocks screaming at dusk.

reftin4.tip: Endless "tink-tink-tink" or "pop-pop-pop", like a tiny hammer on metal.

grycus1.tip: Very thin, high "tseeeep" calls; easily missed.

knswar1.tip: Loud song from a thicket that speeds up and ends in a trill.

busflu1.tip: Low, mournful hoot at night in forest, like a distant foghorn.

yetwow1.tip: Rapid descending "seee-sip-sip-sip-sip" from high in the forest.

recflu1.tip: Hooting "woo-woo-woo-woo" from dense reeds, often at night; seldom seen.
